note: Times are the agency's normal release time. Holiday weeks shift dates; always check schedule_url for the exact date. Entries with verified:false are standard practice that could not be confirmed on an official page on the verification date.

events.name: EIA Weekly Petroleum Status Report
events.schedule: Wednesdays (later in holiday weeks; week ending Nov 6 2026 was released Thu Nov 12 at 12:00 ET)
events.why_it_matters: Shows U.S. crude, gasoline and distillate stocks, imports and refinery use, which often move oil prices within minutes.

events.name: EIA Weekly Natural Gas Storage Report
events.schedule: Thursdays. 2026 exceptions: Fri Nov 13 10:30 ET; Wed Nov 25 12:00 ET (Thanksgiving)
events.why_it_matters: The weekly change in gas in storage versus expectations is the main weekly driver for natural gas futures.

events.name: API Weekly Statistical Bulletin (crude inventories)
events.agency: American Petroleum Institute (industry group, not government)
events.schedule: Tuesdays, about 4:30 pm ET (Wednesday if Monday is a federal holiday)
events.why_it_matters: An early industry estimate of U.S. inventories, released the evening before the EIA report; it often sets the tone for Wednesday.

events.name: Baker Hughes North America Rig Count
events.schedule: Fridays; Thanksgiving week 2026 moves to Wed Nov 25, Christmas week to Wed Dec 23, New Year week to Wed Dec 30
events.why_it_matters: Counts active drilling rigs, a slow-moving hint about future U.S. oil and gas supply.

events.name: USDA WASDE (World Agricultural Supply and Demand Estimates)
events.agency: USDA Office of the Chief Economist / World Agricultural Outlook Board
events.schedule: Monthly. Next: Thu Dec 10 2026 (2026 dates: Jan 12, Feb 10, Mar 10, Apr 9, May 12, Jun 11, Jul 10, Aug 12, Sep 11, Oct 9, Nov 10, Dec 10)
events.why_it_matters: USDA's monthly crop supply and demand numbers; grain futures often jump or drop sharply at noon.

events.name: USDA Crop Progress
events.schedule: Mondays during the growing season (roughly April to November); Nov 2026 releases: 2, 9, 16, 23, 30
events.why_it_matters: Weekly planting, harvest and crop condition ratings; weak ratings can lift grain prices.

events.name: USDA Weekly Export Sales
events.schedule: Thursdays; Friday in holiday weeks (e.g. Fri Nov 13 and Fri Nov 27 2026)
events.why_it_matters: Shows how much U.S. grain and other farm goods foreign buyers bought last week, a read on demand.

events.name: USDA Grain Stocks, Acreage and Prospective Plantings
events.schedule: Quarterly Grain Stocks (Jan, Mar, Jun, Sep); Prospective Plantings in late March; Acreage at end of June. Exact 2027 dates are on the NASS calendar.
events.why_it_matters: These are the biggest surprise-prone grain reports of the year; planted acres and stored grain reset the supply picture.
events.unverified_reason: The NASS calendar page was only readable for November 2026, so the 2027 dates and the noon ET time were not confirmed.

events.name: CFTC Commitments of Traders (COT)
events.schedule: Fridays (data as of the prior Tuesday). Delayed 2026 releases include Nov 16 and Nov 30; Dec 28 is also delayed.
events.why_it_matters: Shows how big speculators and commercial hedgers are positioned; useful context, but it is a few days old.

events.name: FOMC interest rate decision
events.schedule: 8 meetings a year. Next: Dec 8-9 2026 (decision on Dec 9, with projections). 2027: Jan 26-27, Mar 16-17, Apr 27-28, Jun 8-9, Jul 27-28, Sep 14-15, Oct 26-27, Nov 16-17 (2027 dates tentative).
events.why_it_matters: Rate decisions move the dollar, stocks and gold; the press conference starts about 30 minutes later.
events.unverified_reason: Meeting dates confirmed on the Fed calendar page. The 2:00 pm ET statement time is standard practice but is not printed on that page.

events.name: Consumer Price Index (CPI)
events.schedule: Monthly, usually mid-month. Nov 10 2026 was the October release. The December date was not on the page checked; see the BLS December schedule.
events.why_it_matters: The main inflation gauge; surprises shift rate expectations and move gold, stocks and the dollar.

events.name: Producer Price Index (PPI)
events.schedule: Monthly. Nov 13 2026 was the October release. The December date was not on the page checked.
events.why_it_matters: Wholesale inflation; a smaller mover than CPI but can still shift rate expectations.

events.name: Employment Situation (Non-Farm Payrolls)
events.schedule: Monthly, usually the first Friday. Next: Fri Dec 4 2026 (November data).
events.why_it_matters: The jobs report; often the biggest single-day mover for stocks, gold and the dollar.

events.name: GDP (advance, second and third estimates)
events.schedule: Quarterly. Q3 2026 second estimate Wed Nov 25; third estimate Wed Dec 23. The Q4 advance estimate date (Jan 2027) was not listed.
events.why_it_matters: Measures how fast the economy grew; revisions and surprises move rate expectations.
events.unverified_reason: Dates for Nov and Dec 2026 confirmed. The BEA page does not state the time zone (8:30 is Eastern in normal practice) and did not list the January 2027 advance estimate.

events.name: Personal Income and Outlays (PCE inflation)
events.schedule: Monthly. Wed Nov 25 2026 (October data); Wed Dec 23 2026 (November data).
events.why_it_matters: PCE is the Fed's preferred inflation measure.

events.name: ISM Manufacturing PMI
events.schedule: First business day of the month. Next: Tue Dec 1 2026 (November data).
events.why_it_matters: A survey of factory activity; readings above 50 mean growth and can lift industrial commodities.

events.name: OPEC+ meetings
events.schedule: Irregular. A monthly meeting of the eight-country group and periodic full ministerial meetings; news reports point to late November 2026 (Nov 28-29), not confirmed.
events.why_it_matters: Decisions to raise or cut oil output quotas can move crude sharply, often over a weekend.
events.unverified_reason: OPEC's own site returned an error; dates come only from news reports. Check the OPEC press releases before relying on any date.

events.name: China trade data (commodity imports)
events.agency: General Administration of Customs of China
events.schedule: Monthly preliminary data, usually in the second week of the month; detailed commodity tables follow a few days later.
events.why_it_matters: China is the largest buyer of many commodities; import volumes signal demand strength.
events.unverified_reason: The official release calendar could not be opened (certificate error). Timing is inferred from recent release dates (Mar 10 and Apr 14 2026).
